correctness.rationale: Cox's automorphism theorem gives the covering-group dimension as the sum of the Cox-ring graded-piece dimensions; quotienting by the one-dimensional grading torus yields the submitted formula. Direct weighted-monomial counts give the three special formulas for \(1<a<b\), equal heavy weights and \(a=1\). On the canonical/terminal triangles, monotonicity of \(B_r(m)=\binom{r+m-1}{r-1}\) and the submitted binomial estimates isolate the outer corner, with the terminal \(r=2\) exception checked separately. I independently recomputed graded-piece dimensions by a weight-DP and exhaustively recovered every maximum for \(2\le r\le11\); the frozen verifier was also read.
correctness.risk: The theorem concerns algebraic-group dimension, not finite component structure.

value.rationale: Automorphism dimension is a natural symmetry invariant relevant to moduli quotients. The result gives sharp all-dimensional extrema and equality cases, including a nontrivial boundary exception, rather than merely evaluating isolated weighted projective spaces.
value.risk: No claim is made about maximizing symmetry over all weighted projective spaces.

final_claim: For \(X_{r,a,b}=\mathbb P(1^r,a,b)\), the automorphism-group dimension among canonical members is uniquely maximized at \((2r,3r)\) with the stated binomial formula; among terminal members it is maximized at \((1,1),(1,2)\) with value \(15\) for \(r=2\), and uniquely at \((2r-2,3r-3)\) with the stated binomial formula for \(r\ge3\).
